newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese bureaucrat admits accepting cash - reports.
newsitem.headline: Japanese bureaucrat admits accepting cash - reports.

text.p: Another top Japanese Health Ministry official has reportedly admitted he accepted cash from a businessman, the latest in a series of scandals to hit the new administration of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.

Masaru Wada, Health Ministry councillor in charge of welfare for the elderly, told colleagues he received one million yen ($8,800) in cash in October 1994 from the president of a firm which runs homes for the elderly, according to Japanese media reports on Friday.
The president of the company, Hiroshi Koyama, was arrested two weeks ago on bribery charges involving officials of the Health Ministry.

Vice Health Minister Nobuharu Okamitsu resigned on November 19 after partially admitting media accusations that he took gifts from Koyama. But he denied taking cash from him and has not been linked to the bribery charge levelled against Koyama.
Okamitsu is currently being questioned by authorities, the Health Ministry said.
"I returned the money to Koyama in the summer of last year. I haven't granted favours to anybody," Wada allegedly said.
A Health Ministry spokesman said Wada was unavailable for comment as he was on leave on Friday and it was not known if he would return to work next week.

Wada is responsible for a bill requiring local governments to provide full health care for the extremely ill and elderly, which was scheduled to be submitted at the extraordinary session of parliament that opened on Friday.
The bill is important for Hashimoto's cabinet, which took office in early November, and the news could affect the bill's chances in parliament.
Hashimoto expressed his concern on Friday, saying: "It makes me wonder whether there is still more of this sort of thing happening."
But he said the case should be viewed separately from the proposed legislation.

The Health Ministry scandal is not the only one involving the government. Officials at the powerful Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) are being investigated over possible ties to an Osaka oil dealer who made large donations to politicians and bureaucrats.
